item.title: Molecular Gas Optics Using Vibrational Population Density Refraction
item.description: arXiv:2611.13242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gas optics holds promise for development of advanced optical elements with 2-3 orders of magnitude higher damage threshold than any solid-state optics. Here, we demonstrate a new concept for refracting the laser beam using vibrationally excited molecules as gas optics instead of traditional control of thermodynamic gas temperature. The transient, vibrational population density grating is formed in a CO2 gas by interfering two mid-IR lasers to imprint spatial modulation in the linear refractive index (Delta n0 >=2x10-5) of the neutral gas via enhancement of the molecular polarizability. It is increased by pumping the asymmetric stretching mode of CO2 at optimal wavelengths to resonantly produce a highly nonequilibrium state that increases the effective vibrational mode temperature to greater than 2000 K in a room temperature gas. The measured beam steering efficiency of such a volume gas grating exceeds 90% that makes this approach a candidate for producing other large-aperture, high-throughput molecular optics elements, with expected damage thresholds 0.5-1 kJ/cm2, much-needed for future ultrahigh-power lasers.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Matteo, Sergei Tochitsky, Chan Joshi

item.title: Hysteresis and mode switching in FIB engineered random laser diodes
item.description: arXiv:2611.13328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex dynamical behavior in laser diodes is commonly induced by external perturbations such as optical or optoelectronic feedback and optical injection. The structural transformation of a stable laser diode into a stand-alone nonlinear dynamical system would provide a practical alternative as a single and compact device. Here we demonstrate the fabrication of such a device by milling, via focused ion beam, the output facet of a Fabry-Perot laser diode with a predesigned mask, obtaining a scattering surface which provide feedback for random lasing. The fabricated random laser diode shows multi-mode emission with current dependent spectral reconfigurations, hysteresis in output power and spectrum and mode switching at constant bias current. We attribute this behavior to the interplay between scattered optical feedback and carrier induced local variations of refractive index and temperature at the output facet surface, where defects are located. The observed phenomena reveal complex nonlinear behavior emerging from a single standalone device, which could be tailored by varying the milling pattern, thereby providing a flexible platform for different applications.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Mart\'inez Pacheco, Sara Rodr\'iguez Corvillo, Alberto Rivera-Calzada, Antonio Consoli, Jacobo Santamar\'ia, Cefe L\'opez

item.title: Universal spectral shapes of nonlinear light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings
item.description: arXiv:2611.13341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operating within the framework of the collisionless Boltzmann equation, we identify universal spectral profiles inherent in stimulated and coherent light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings and derive physically intuitive solutions for such spectral shapes, expressing them in a manifestly causal closed form that satisfies the Kramers - Kronig relations and fulfills the fluctuation - dissipation theorem. Benchmarking against gold-standard experiments on dilute-gas stimulated light scattering verifies a high descriptive and explanatory power of these solutions and demonstrates their ability to isolate universality motifs in nonlinear scattering spectra as the key to fully understanding the physics behind dilute-gas nonlinear light scattering. As one of important outcomes, such analysis reveals the physical content of the bandwidth of dilute-gas nonlinear scattering spectra as an expression and a quantifier of the phase-mixing time, i.e., the time required for free-streaming gas particles with a mean thermal velocity to traverse the distance equal to the spacing of the laser-driven density grating.
item.dc:creator: Aleksei Zheltikov

item.title: Hopfion Superlattices in 3D Twisted Moir\'e Light Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.13476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e superlattices have recently been extended from electronic materials to photonic systems, enabling complex topological light fields such as skyrmion bags. However, these realizations remain confined to two dimensions. Here, we demonstrate 3D moir\'e superlattices formed by twisting multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices, giving rise to previously undiscovered 3D quasiparticle topologies, including hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and hopfion-hopfionium nested superlattices. By tailoring the interference polarization textures of the moir\'e spacetime lattices, we achieve controlled topological transitions among these states, and tailored topological numbers of hopfion bags. These spatiotemporal supertopologies offer a promising platform for high-capacity information encoding in higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Zhang, Vasu Dev, Yijie Shen

item.title: Development of a versatile modular system to study the ablation and plume expansion in a thin film
item.description: arXiv:2611.13570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-resolved investigation of laser ablation of thin films requires stable, repeatable, and efficient experimental environment. Conventional approaches often rely on multiple laser-ablation shots acquired at different delay times to reconstruct the temporal evolution of the process, thereby assuming shot-to-shot reproducibility. This work presents a novel modular experimental setup that addresses these challenges and enables a systematic pump--probe study of laser--matter interaction. The setup provides reliable single-pulse measurements with controlled sample positioning inside the high vacuum chamber, as well as integrated data recording, which improves redundancy and ease with which experiments can be performed. Further, the setup serves as an advanced diagnostic tool for investigating the time evolution of laser--matter interactions, ablation dynamics and laser-produced plasmas in a single laser shot, in various configurations with a temporal resolution better than 15 ns. Using this capability, we show that for a fixed ablation geometry, the transient reflectivity and transmission response depends strongly on the probing side, indicating that probing direction is an independent diagnostic variable whose omission can lead to incomplete or misleading picture of the ablation dynamics. This experimental technique can advance the understanding of surface modification and plume expansion, which are relevant to fundamental studies and also for range of applications, including laser cleaning of tokamak viewports and mirrors, pulsed laser deposition (PLD), surface structuring and laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT), among others. The present setup is versatile enough to perform these studies under different ablation configurations without implementing major changes in the experimental configuration.
item.dc:creator: Renjith Kumar R, Pabitra Kumar Mishra, B R Geethika, Hem C Joshi, Jinto Thomas

item.title: Revisiting the dispersions and quality factors of nanoshell plasmons
item.description: arXiv:2611.13589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dispersions and quality factors of a metallic nanoshell's plasmons may be readily tuned by varying the thickness of the nanoshell. This is because 1. Thickness determines the hybridization between the two nanoshell boundaries and 2. Thickness affects the electronic surface scattering rate and, therefore, the non-radiative decay rates of the plasmonic resonances. We find that prior theoretical works, focused primarily on the thin-nanoshell and retarded regimes, obtained qualitatively incorrect results for both the plasmonic dispersions and the associated plasmonic quality factors. Some of these errors have been pointed out in subsequent works, though the corrected results have not been reported, to our knowledge. Beyond obtaining the correct results (correct dispersions and quality factors as a function of nanoshell thickness), we scrutinize the assumption (used by many prior works) that Matthiessen's rule may be used to combine the effects of bulk and surface-mediated plasmonic scattering processes. To do so, we extend prior work by Dingle to the nanoshell geometry. Although we find qualitative agreement with the Matthiessen's rule approach, we find that Dingle's theory systematically predicts higher quality factors across the range of nanoshell thicknesses we consider.
item.dc:creator: Ali Ghorashi, Victoria Zhang

item.title: Overcoming Dynamic Range Limitations in Computational Hyperspectral Imaging
item.description: arXiv:2611.13663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational hyperspectral imaging offers compact spectral sensing, yet imaging high-dynamic-range (HDR) scenes remains challenging. Accurate spectral reconstruction requires encoded measurements to remain within the calibrated linear-response range and above the noise floor. Due to unequal spectral responsivities across the encoding mask, individual channels reach their reliability limits at vastly different incident signal levels. Measurement reliability therefore depends on both exposure time and encoding channel, making it challenging for a single exposure to preserve spectral information in highlights and shadows simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate a physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework that operates directly in the encoded measurement domain. An analytical reliability prior and learned spatially varying, channel-specific adjustments jointly determine adaptive fusion weights. Measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision further constrains relative channel responses for downstream spectral inversion. The set-wise formulation accommodates varying numbers and configurations of input exposures. We further implement the framework on a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera, incorporating full-field sensor-response characterization and channel-aware reliability gating. Simulated HDR benchmarks show lower reconstruction errors than representative fusion methods, while controlled spectral measurements and practical HDR scenes confirm improved spectral fidelity and extended usable dynamic range. Measurements using an optical-density target further establish a 16.0-dB increase in spectral reconstruction dynamic range relative to the best fixed single exposure.
item.dc:creator: Qianqian Yu, Jinhang Lin, Zhihai Yao, Shuo Wang, Chaofan Weng, Xiang Hao

item.title: Stress-controlled avoided-crossing evolution of an optical microresonator induced by inter-fibre side coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.13722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analogies between quantum mechanics and photonics provide a powerful means of transferring concepts and phenomena between the two fields. Photonic analogues offer a distinctive advantage by allowing us to engineer and continuously vary parameters fixed by the microscopic structure of quantum systems, revealing richer behaviour. Building on these analogies, the recent demonstration of widely tunable microresonators formed by side coupling between optical fibres marked a significant advance in the development of reconfigurable resonant photonic systems. However, those methods offered no direct way to reach the centre of the avoided crossing, where the uncoupled fibre cutoff frequencies coincide and the modes hybridise most strongly. Here, we introduce an additional tuning degree of freedom by axially stretching a straight fibre coupled to a bent fibre. At essentially fixed coupling geometry, this lets us sweep the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero. As the avoided crossing is approached, the induced microresonator's resonance band widens. Beyond the crossing, the band narrows and, strikingly, appears to "hang" below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency. Our experimental results agree with coupled-mode theory and indicate the feasibility of 100 MHz-scale control of the straight-fibre cutoff frequency and the resonator spectral height over a tuning range of about 100 GHz, using a relative elongation of order $10^{-3}$.
item.dc:creator: Isha Sharma, Misha Sumetsky

item.title: Structural Perturbations and Full Field Evolution in Tapered Spun Ring-Core Fiber Amplifiers
item.description: arXiv:2611.13743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate the complex full-vector modal field evolution in tapered spun ring-core fiber amplifiers subject to structural perturbations, utilizing a combined coupled-mode theory and rate-equation model. To provide a comprehensive characterization, we introduce a normalized complex modal-state fidelity factor that simultaneously incorporates intensity, phase and polarization into a single quantitative measure. We demonstrate that the twist pitch of the structure can be purposely tuned to either suppress or leverage the effect of specific geometrical perturbations. These findings provide insight into the physical conditions governing modal stability, establishing a robust mechanism for highly efficient in-fiber OAM mode conversion.
item.dc:creator: Hassan Asgharzadeh B., Regina Gumenyuk, Marco Ornigotti

item.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
item.description: arXiv:2611.13746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang, Xiaoyu Guan, Jinbo Zhao, Yuting Guo, Zhihao Li, Zirui Li, Tengyu Ma, Ying Tang, Zhe Li, Weiwei Zuo, Jorge Pascual, Bo Hou, Feng Yang, Xiaoli Pan, Yu Wang, Luyao Wang, Lin-Long Deng, Guixiang Li, Luca Sapienza, Antonio Abate, Meng Li

item.title: Time-Varying Photonics: A Review of Theory, Phenomena, and Experimental Platforms
item.description: arXiv:2611.13764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-varying photonics opens new avenues for controlling waves through engineering material properties in time. In this review, we introduce the basic concepts and theoretical tools for describing temporal interfaces, time-periodic systems, and space-time media, as well as review representative experimental approaches across different photonic and wave platforms. We further discuss characteristic phenomena enabled by temporal modulation, including coherent wave control, parametric amplification, nonreciprocity, and topological effects. This review provides a unified pathway for understanding time-varying photonics and outlines its current challenges and future opportunities in both fundamental physics and practical applications.
item.dc:creator: Zhaohui Dong, Xianfeng Chen, Luqi Yuan

item.title: An Alignment Microscope for Imaging Rotational Wavepacket Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.14034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new method for encoding polarization-angle-dependent molecular alignment signals directly into the transverse spatial profile of a femtosecond laser beam. The approach employs a pump-probe setup in a common-path geometry. A radial-azimuthal polarization converter placed in the probe beam produces a doughnut-shaped beam whose local polarization varies continuously with azimuthal angle, thereby encoding the full range of linear polarization orientations from 0 to $2\pi$ within a single transverse beam profile. Consequently, the angular dependence of the molecular response can be recorded simultaneously rather than reconstructed through sequential measurements at different polarization angles. By varying only the pump-probe delay, this spatial encoding enables single-shot acquisition of the complete angular response at each delay and real-time visualization of the evolving molecular alignment pattern as the delay stage is scanned. This technique has enabled the experimental realization of an alignment microscope.
item.dc:creator: J. Strohaber

item.title: SGAA: Independent active alignment of optical subgroups with uncompensated aberrations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncompensated subgroup aberrations complicate subgroup-level active alignment (AA), as local image-quality extrema do not directly indicate the target alignment state. We propose SGAA, an image-learning-based method for independent active alignment of optical subgroups. Multi-field point spread functions (PSFs) from a dedicated test configuration characterize misalignment, while golden-sample reference calibration and unified regression predict adjustments toward a common optical target across toleranced specimens. In simulations with tolerances, one step reduced the mean differential wavefront RMS from $0.0592\lambda$ to $0.0086\lambda$, an 85.4% reduction. In alignment experiments on 100 production subgroups, SGAA increased the mean full-lens weighted modulation transfer function (WMTF) at 30, 50, and 80 lp/mm by 0.073, 0.065, and 0.040, respectively, relative to industrial MTF-based scanning. The 8 MP acceptance yield increased by 29.2 percentage points, and mean alignment time decreased from 43 s to 3.1 s. SGAA thus translates independent subgroup reference-state restoration into gains in full-lens imaging, acceptance yield, and alignment speed.
item.dc:creator: Le Dai, Zhenyao Zheng, Wenyong Li, Yuhan Bao, Weijian Hu, Kailun Yang, Kaiwei Wang

item.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases
item.description: arXiv:2611.14119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases is essential for attosecond science. Improving conversion efficiency from the infrared driving laser to the extreme-ultraviolet high-order harmonic radiation requires balancing microscopic single-atom dipole responses with macroscopic phase matching. The resulting conversion-efficiency landscape exhibits complex structures, such as the hyperbolic ridge in the pressure-length space, which can be difficult to accurately reconstruct using conventional Bayesian optimization. Here, we introduce a physics-informed Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates known physical scaling relations through nonlinear transformations of the search space. We first demonstrate the approach in the two-dimensional pressure-length space, where a direct grid scan enables detailed validation of the reconstructed landscape, before extending it to four dimensions, where exhaustive scanning becomes computationally impractical. In four dimensions, incorporating the pulse-duration scaling and a square-root transformation of conversion efficiency further improves the accuracy of the reconstructed landscape, as validated against an independent reference dataset. We also employ a threshold-based acquisition strategy to identify extended high-efficiency operating regions rather than isolated optimal points. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating physical knowledge into Bayesian optimization improves the exploration and reconstruction of multidimensional high-order harmonic generation landscapes, extending its capabilities beyond locating individual optima.
item.dc:creator: Dominika Maslarova, Mattys Pouyez, Patrik Jansson, Jan Vabek, Robin Weissenbilder, Linus Hagedorn, Anne L'Huillier, T\"unde F\"ul\"op

item.title: Exponential Control of Adiabatic Time Reflection by Complex-Time Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.14133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nearly identical temporal switching profiles can produce very different reflections even when both have small local adiabatic measures. In a lossless dielectric, we obtain this difference by adding a weak feature that changes the complex-time singularities while preserving monotonicity, endpoints, and central slope. A perturbation bounded by $0.6\%$ of the total inverse-permittivity change raises the reflected mode amplitude from $8.02\times10^{-10}$ to $1.28\times10^{-3}$. The complex action and pole residue predict this amplitude to within $0.32\%$. Within this waveform family, deviation and monotonicity constraints select three design regimes. At fixed deviation bound, reoptimization keeps the central feature's time scale comparable to the inverse incident angular frequency. The optimal amplitude is then proportional to $1/T$ as the switching time $T$ tends to infinity. Stretching a fixed profile gives exponential suppression. Full-wave Maxwell simulations resolve the backward packet, and filtering calculations quantify its sensitivity to modulation bandwidth.
item.dc:creator: Shiyue Deng, Qian Niu

item.title: Intracycle Interference in Strong-Field Photoemission from a Tungsten Needle Tip
item.description: arXiv:2611.14205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrons photoemitted by strong laser fields can rescatter, generating attosecond high harmonics. Spectral peaks arise from inter- and intracycle interference of coherent electron wave packets. While intercycle interference is well known, intracycle interference of plateau electrons has not been observed. We present carrier-envelope phase-resolved photoemission spectra from a nanometric tungsten needle tip driven at 1570 nm revealing such interference, supported by quantum orbit and TDSE simulations that elucidate attosecond-scale electron dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Timo Wirth, Jonas Heimerl, Stefan Meier, Peter Hommelhoff

item.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.14293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.
item.dc:creator: Lei Hou, Xiang Zhang, Qiang Zhu, Xiang-Pei Liu, Fa-Xi Chen, Wen-Xuan Song, Zhuan-Xian Xiong, Jian-Yu Guan, Yu-Chen Zhang, De-Quan Kong, Jia-Hao Zhang, Long-Fei Liao, Shao-Mao Wang, Bing Wang, De-Zhi Xiong, Xing-Yang Cui, Ping Xu, Peng Liu, Jie Li, Xiao Jiang, Hua-Qing Zhang, Ling-Xiang He, Li-Bo Li, Qi Shen, Youchao Xie, Lei Wang, Sheng-Kai Liao, Juan Yin, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Wen-Bin Shen, Baolong Lyu, Han-Ning Dai, Qiang Zhang, Yu-Ao Chen, Hai-Feng Jiang, Jian-Wei Pan

item.title: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics at 493 nm
item.description: arXiv:2611.14474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visible and near-ultraviolet light underpins applications from biophotonics to quantum computing, which demand fast control of optical amplitude and phase. Integrated photonics offers scalable control, yet most visible-wavelength platforms lack gigahertz-scale modulation. We demonstrate a thin-film lithium niobate platform at 493 nm integrating grating couplers, beamsplitters, ring resonators, and modulators. Segmented traveling-wave modulators achieve a half-wave voltage--length product of 450 mV$\cdot$cm, $>$20 dB extinction, and bandwidth beyond 50 GHz. Ring resonators show $2.9 \pm 0.2$ dB/cm propagation loss and quantify the platform's photorefractive response. This enables agile visible beam delivery for trapped-ion systems, although photorefraction and substrate uniformity remain key challenges to scaling.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Achuthan, Let\'icia Magalh\~aes, Xudong Li, Hugo Voncken, Hana Warner, Sophie Ding, Andrea Cordaro, Xinrui Zhu, Keith Powell, Anna Shelton, Dylan Renaud, Daniel Assumpcao, Xiangying Zuo, Michael Pushkarsky, Amirhassan Shams-Ansari, Marko Lon\v{c}ar

item.title: Background-free and laser-ionization minimized single-shot fs-EFISH in luminous pulsed plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2611.13158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work introduces spectrally tuned electric field induced second harmonic (t-EFISH) generation for substantially reducing or eliminating background plasma emission in single-shot, time-resolved, electric field measurements. The technique is demonstrated using a femtosecond 1240 nm pump and 620 nm signal detection to avoid spectral and temporal overlap with the early, intense onset of N2(C-B) emission in nanosecond atmospheric-pressure air spark discharges. This enhances signal-to-emission ratios pre- and post-breakdown, enables lower pump energies, suppresses detector saturation, and reduces the coefficient of variation in the electric field measurements by 8.5x. This strategy also provides a pathway for background-free measurements in other discharge environments with varying spectro-temporal emission characteristics. Moreover, the longer 1240 nm pump wavelength reduces multiphoton intrusiveness, directly improving measurement fidelity.
item.dc:creator: Vidyadhara B. V. Kumar, Karna Patel, Aman Satija, Sally Bane, Terrence R. Meyer

item.title: Multicomponent Isotope Engineering of Phonon Polaritons in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
item.description: arXiv:2611.13319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Isotopic enrichment provides a non-invasive means of tuning the vibrational and optical properties of van der Waals crystals (vdW) without altering their lattice structure. We investigate two doubly enriched hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) compositions, h10B15N and h11B15N, to determine how isotope substitution on both sublattices modifies mid-infrared hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs). Polarization-resolved room temperature and cryogenic far-field reflectance measurements reveal optical-phonon blue shifts of approximately 35 cm-1 in h10B15N relative h11B15N, translating both Reststrahlen bands (RBs) and their polariton dispersions. For the upper RB, the combined accessible range expands from 1360-1614 cm-1 in natural hBN to 1356-1640 cm-1 across the B- enriched 14N crystals and 1339-1640 cm-1 when the 15N enriched crystals are included. Near-field imaging confirms deeply sub-diffractional propagation and shows that both crystals exhibit lower polariton damping and longer lifetimes than natural hBN, with performance comparable to monoisotopically enriched crystals. Further, we compare the conventional reduced-mass description with a phenomenological two-component inverse-mass model that captures the isotope dependence of the phonon frequencies and LO-TO coupling while resolving the contributions of the individual sublattices. These results establish multicomponent isotope engineering as a materials design strategy for positioning the HPhPs spectral range while preserving low-loss propagation in polar vdW crystals.
item.dc:creator: Nihar Ranjan Sahoo, Byung-Il Noh, Brandon Stephanie, Hossein Zandipour, Eli Janzen, James H. Edgar, Siyuan Dai, Thomas G. Folland

item.title: Optically modulated field-dependent electrical response in a non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.13351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interplay among optical, electrical, and magnetic stimuli offers opportunities to control the functional response of spintronic heterostructures. Here, we investigate the field-dependent electrical response of MgO/IrMn$_3$/Py/Au under radio-frequency (RF) excitation, white-light illumination, and direct-current (DC) bias. Under a 20 MHz RF signal with a nominal power of 2 W, the measured voltage in the dark remains at several tens of nanovolts. Upon illumination with approximately 1 W of white light, a pronounced field-dependent feature emerges around 315--320 Oe, reaching 0.9--1.0 $\mu$V. The illumination-associated differential voltage is approximately 0.95 $\mu$V. A DC current of 1 mA produces a response of approximately 1 $\mu$V, while the simultaneous application of RF, DC, and optical excitation increases the voltage to approximately 1.8 $\mu$V. Magnetic characterization reveals exchange bias with a blocking temperature near 380 K, while electrical resistance measurements show a pronounced dependence on magnetic-field orientation, consistent with the anisotropic response of the heterostructure. These results demonstrate that the field-dependent electrical response can be modulated through combined optical and electrical excitation, involving magneto-optical interactions and spin-dependent transport phenomena, potentially including spin Hall-related contributions and the magnetic spin Hall effect. This work provides insights into coupled optical, electrical, and magnetic-field effects in heterostructures based on non-collinear antiferromagnets and ferromagnetic layers.
item.dc:creator: Adrielson Dias, Andr\'e Jos\'e, Jos\'e Lucas, Rodrigo Cristian, Jos\'e Holanda

item.title: Additively manufactured ceramic platforms for miniaturized optical frequency references and robust atomic sensor systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.13800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transferring atomic quantum sensors from laboratory-scale physics packages to compact, alignment-free sensor heads suitable for field and space deployment requires a structural platform that combines mechanical, thermal, and optical functionality within a single, manufacturable component. We present such a platform based on additively manufactured technical ceramics: lithography-based ceramic manufacturing is used to fabricate monolithic micro-optical benches with application-specific mounting geometries, while high-precision active alignment and adhesive bonding realize long-term stable optical assemblies through micro-integration. As a first system-level demonstrator, we present a micro-integrated optical frequency reference based on Doppler-free spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 line, integrated within a 6 mL Al2O3 module. A laser stabilized to the reference reaches a fractional frequency instability of $3\times10^{-12}$ at 1 s. We extend the platform to a compact optically pumped magnetometer, exploiting the magnetic cleanliness and tailored thermal properties of high-purity ceramics for a 7 mL sensor head with picotesla sensitivity aimed at space-borne biomagnetometry, and to a micro-integrated optical dipole trap with active MEMS-mirror beam steering for cold-atom manipulation. Together, these demonstrators show that ceramic additive manufacturing and optical micro-integration form a versatile, robust platform for compact atomic sensor systems in field and space applications.
item.dc:creator: Marc Christ, Sascha Neinert, Conrad Zimmermann, Klaus D\"oringshoff, Markus Krutzik

item.title: Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance
item.description: arXiv:2611.13936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. Detuning can carry the material path through narrow resonances, producing intermittent rather than sustained power growth. For an explicit family of noncircular shells and a smooth exterior dipole source, both fixed, we classify the dissipated power under a quantitative smallness condition on the deformation. Depending on the detuning exponent and conformal source distance, the power diverges along the entire path, exhibits divergent peaks with vanishing gaps, or decays, including the threshold cases. We also identify the sharp conformal boundary beyond which the field, normalized by the square root of the dissipated power, converges locally to zero along every divergent-power sequence. For resonant sources, tangential reference crossings yield an explicit nonzero limit for the exterior gradient energy divided by the dissipated power at the critical radius.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Alexopoulos

item.title: CV-TF-QKD
item.description: arXiv:2611.14044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution, using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Full-record reconciliation and a binary phase-disclosure protocol achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. At fixed weak input-referred excess noise per arm, both rates per relay use scale as $\sqrt{\eta}$, where $\eta$ is the end-to-end transmissivity. For phase disclosure, we establish composable security against general coherent attacks using a bounded test of preparation intensities and sign-parity complementarity. For specified apparatus parameters, finite-key calculations incorporating detector inefficiency, dark counts, phase fluctuations, and reference overhead predict rates exceeding the pure-loss and matched thermal-loss repeaterless bounds. These results extend the twin-field advantage to Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum cryptography.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
item.description: arXiv:2611.14447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths. To illustrate the capabilities of the setup, we present results for rough aluminum and stainless-steel surfaces as reference materials. Fitting the measured angular profiles with the analytical GGX microfacet model allows us to extract the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index and the surface roughness parameter of each sample. These parameters are then used to extrapolate the in-plane measurements to the full hemisphere and from gaseous argon to liquid media, enabling the inference of the hemispherical reflectance in gaseous argon, liquid argon and liquid xenon.
item.dc:creator: H. Amar, J. \'Alvarez, X. Arrue, C. Benitez, A. Cervera-Villanueva, J. Mart\'in-Albo, L. Molina-Bueno, A. Roche, M. Sorel, J. Soto-Oton, S. Teruel-Pardo, N. Yahlali

item.title: Stability and optical quality of "windmill"-formed 8CB liquid crystal films for replenishable plasma mirrors
item.description: arXiv:2509.18448v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Liquid crystal (LC) film plasma mirrors (PMs) based on 4-octyl-4'-cyanobiphenyl (8CB) are an enabling technology for reflecting high-fluence laser pulses. These freestanding LC films can achieve high optical quality and are well-suited for rep-rated applications, as motorized devices continuously replenish films over an aperture following each destructive laser shot. However, a systematic characterization of film quality as a function of seminal operating conditions had not yet been performed for the LC "windmill" version of the device, which aims to match the repetition rate of an existing "spinning disk" (SDI) version and the angular stability of the "linear slider" (LSTI) version. We determined the 8CB film quality using low-power wavefront measurements, and studied the film-to-film wavefront stability and formation reliability. The film-formation reliability of 8CB LC films demonstrated 97\% formation success at 2.7 mm/s film-forming speeds, but decreased to 45\% at 10.8 mm/s. These reliability numbers will inform future designs to reach Hz-level repetition rates and beyond. Depending on area-of-interest within the 10 mm diameter film, the added wavefront root-mean-squared (RMS) variation was as small as 10 nm for a 2 mm diameter region, and $<$50 nm for a 3 mm diameter region. Within the optimal 21-22$^\circ$C operating regime, pointing fluctuations remained at or below 0.52 mrad. With a maximum effective film formation frequency of \textasciitilde0.25 Hz, these results establish windmill-formed 8CB films as promising candidates to pursue next-iteration improvements towards rep-rated plasma-mirror operation.

item.title: Exponentially enhanced sensing through non-reciprocal light propagation
item.description: arXiv:2511.16895v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-reciprocity is a key resource for pushing the performance of photonic devices beyond the fundamental limits imposed by Lorentz reciprocity. Notably, it was predicted that sensor architectures implementing a bosonic analogue of the Kitaev chain can yield an enhanced signal-to-noise ratio. However, experimental demonstrations of such sensors have so far been limited to small chains. Here we show how this model can be implemented in a scalable optical platform, enabling the detection of weak perturbations with a signal-to-noise ratio, linked to the quantum Fisher information extracted per input photon, that grows exponentially with system size. Our approach encodes two coupled Hatano-Nelson chains---realizing an effective bosonic Kitaev model---within the resonant modes of an electro-optic frequency comb. Non-reciprocal propagation in frequency space is achieved via simultaneous phase and amplitude modulation of the intracavity field. We demonstrate the sensing of a weak modulation tone coupling the two chains, observing an exponential enhancement of the signal-to-noise over three orders of magnitude as the system is scaled to over 70 frequency modes per chain. These results establish a new regime of non-Hermitian sensing, highlighting how non-reciprocal dynamics can be harnessed to achieve exponentially enhanced measurement precision in photonic systems.
item.dc:creator: Paul-\'Edouard Blanchard, Alexander McDonald, Philippe St-Jean

item.title: Infrared light scattering and emission from epsilon near-zero hyperbolic phonon-polaritons in two-dimensional crystals
item.description: arXiv:2608.15771v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents the near-field super-scattering and the near-field thermal emission from 2D hyperbolic crystals as general optical phenomena that link near-field nanophotonics to far-field photonics.

item.title: From OpenSPIM to FlowSPIM: Enhancing the versatility of a light-sheet microscope through an iterative design process
item.description: arXiv:2609.31115v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Light-sheet microscopy is ideal for the 3D imaging of large biological specimens, yet systematic documentation on adapting microscope designs to diverse experimental requirements remains limited. We present the iterative process used to design and build a modular light-sheet microscope and adapt it to different sample types and experimental conditions, including live and fixed zebrafish, Drosophila, and mouse gastruloids, as well as cellulose nanocrystals. Starting from a stripped-down OpenSPIM platform, we gradually made our microscope more versatile by adding hardware such as additional laser channels and optical filters, and new protocols for sample handling. In its final iteration, FlowSPIM is a new flow-based incubation technique for 3D tissue culture.

item.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.08733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU and an operational figure of merit of 40 $\mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$, this low-loss HfO$_{2}$ metasurface provides a robust foundation for label-free DUV biosensing.
item.dc:creator: Be\'ata Idesov\'a, Alexander A. Antonov, Lina Rohrer, Leonardo de Souza Menezes, Andreas Tittl, Tom\'a\v{s} \v{S}ikola, Filip Ligmajer

item.title: Intensity limits for phase-only holographic optical-tweezer arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.10302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optical tweezers use tightly focused laser beams to trap and manipulate individual particles, enabling advances in quantum computing, drug discovery, and biological research. Scaling these technologies to large arrays requires delivering sufficient light to every trapping site while minimizing the total laser power required. Here, we investigate the fundamental limits of how efficiently a phase-only hologram can distribute light across an array of optical traps. We derive upper bounds on the minimum intensity across trapping sites, accounting for illumination, target geometry, and diffraction from spatial light modulator pixels. For arrays arranged in a single plane or across two axial planes, we show how these limits scale with the number of traps and SLM pixels, and establish conditions for focusing light in three dimensions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that optimized holograms can closely approach these theoretical limits, suggesting that further improvements in phase optimization alone offer limited power savings. Instead, our results reveal how the choice of illumination and trap geometry can improve light efficiency, providing practical guidelines for designing larger, more power-efficient optical-tweezer arrays.
item.dc:creator: Anzhou Wen, Hengyu Lian, Kevin Yipu Wu, Maxwell F. Parsons, Praneeth Chakravarthula

item.title: Wide Field 3D Color Topography for Steep-slope Structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.11797v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) topography measurement is essential for industrial inspection and scientific research. However, existing techniques are limited by an inherent trade-off between resolution, speed, color imaging capability and the ability to measure large-angle surfaces. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel method that integrates ring light illumination based wide-field 3D imaging with an iterative shape-from-focus (SFF) algorithm. The system employs coaxial epi-illumination combined with ring light illumination to simultaneously acquire information from flat regions and steep slopes. The proposed iterative SFF algorithm achieves high-resolution 3D topography measurement. Full-color 3D reconstructions of electronic chips and PCBs demonstrate that the proposed method enables fast scanning and sub-micrometer resolution and significantly extending the measurable inclination range for large-angle structures. This method fills a critical gap in existing technology for fast, natural-color, 3D imaging and measurement of samples with steep topographies.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Lin, Mengrui Wang, Fan Li, Jingxiang Zhang, Manming Shu, Jiajing Yan, Chang Liu, Tianyu Zhao, Yansheng Liang, Ming Lei

item.title: Silicon and silicon nitride photonic ring resonator arrays for photonic trimming metrology
item.description: arXiv:2611.12154v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Proposed silicon on silicon oxide 4x4 matrix multiplier for use in refractive index measurements, based on the Advanced Micro Foundry deep ultraviolet process. Agreement between simulated spectra and analytic design spectra demonstrate the intended performance of the components given a 1550 nm wavelength spectrum analysis. Intended purpose of the design includes optical damage analysis of the cladding, and photonic chip refractive index analysis following sub-threshold laser ablation. Femtosecond multi-shot tuning of refractive index is not a recommended application, due to round trip-losses causing quality factor and transfer function degradation.
item.dc:creator: Cael Warner

item.title: Off-focus detection for SNR enhancement in coherent single-pixel imaging
item.description: arXiv:2611.12238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherent single-pixel imaging (CSPI) enables amplitude- and phase-resolved computational imaging with a single coherent detector, offering particular advantages in spectral regimes where high-performance detector arrays remain unavailable. In conventional Fourier-plane CSPI, the detector is typically placed at the focal point to maximize the collected power. However, this focal position does not necessarily maximize the reconstruction fidelity for image reconstruction in the presence of system nonidealities. Here, we introduce detector position as an additional degree of freedom for CSPI optimization. We show that appropriately selected off-focus Fourier-plane positions can improve reconstruction performance by suppressing fluctuation-sensitive coherent backgrounds while preserving spatially encoded signals. Experimentally, using a programmable liquid-crystal terahertz spatial light modulator and coherent heterodyne detection, we demonstrate improved amplitude and phase reconstruction from selected off-focus channels compared with focal detection. A symmetric off-focus pair with complementary transverse-wave-vector weighting further enhances image fidelity, contrast, and compressive-sampling robustness through coherent channel fusion. These results establish detector-position engineering as a new strategy for enhancing the robustness and information efficiency of CSPI.
item.dc:creator: Wei Zhu, Hui Yuan, Hangbing Guo, Sheng Wang, Da Tian, Benwen Chen, Kebin Fan, Caihong Zhang, Huabing Wang, Biaobing Jin, Jian Chen, Peiheng Wu, Hartmut G. Roskos, Jingbo Wu

item.title: Plasmascopy of ultrafast hot charge carriers
item.description: arXiv:2512.05582v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We demonstrate an electric-field-resolved approach for probing ultrafast dynamics of photoinjected charge carriers in solids. Direct access to the electric field of few cycle pulses enables us to measure a broadband response of a medium with associated plasma frequency. We prepare an ensemble of hot charge carriers with energies sufficient to trigger impact ionization and establish a framework to measure its dynamics. Our time-resolved study reveals the short-lived ultrafast dynamics consistent with impact ionization and carrier trapping. This approach provides a promising route for studying ultrafast many-body physics in photoexcited solids, with predictions from advanced theoretical models.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry A. Zimin, Raja Sen, Muhammad Qasim, Jelena Sjakste, Vladislav S. Yakovlev

item.title: Below-shot-noise capacity in phase estimation using nonlinear interferometers
item.description: arXiv:2601.04139v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Over the past decade, several schemes for imaging and sensing based on nonlinear interferometers have been proposed and demonstrated experimentally. These interferometers exhibit two main advantages. First, they enable probing a sample at a chosen wavelength while detecting light at a different wavelength with high efficiency (bicolor quantum imaging and sensing with undetected light). Second, they can show quantum-enhanced sensitivities below the shot-noise limit, potentially reaching Heisenberg-limited precision in parameter estimation. Here, we compare three quantum-imaging configurations using only easily accessible intensity-based measurements for phase estimation: a Yurke-type SU(1,1) interferometer, a Mandel-type induced-coherence interferometer, and a hybrid scheme that continuously interpolates between them. While an ideal Yurke interferometer can exhibit Heisenberg scaling, this advantage is known to be fragile under realistic detection constraints and in the presence of loss. We demonstrate that differential intensity detection in the Mandel interferometer provides the highest and most robust phase sensitivity among the considered schemes, reaching but not surpassing the shot-noise limit, even in the presence of loss. Intensity measurements in a Yurke-type configuration can achieve genuine sub-shot-noise sensitivity under balanced losses and moderate gain; however, their performance degrades in realistic high-gain regimes. Consequently, in this regime, the Mandel configuration with differential detection outperforms the Yurke-type setup and constitutes the most robust approach for phase estimation.
item.dc:creator: Cristofero Oglialoro, Gerard J. Machado, Felix Farsch, Daniel F. Urrego, Alejandra A. Padilla, Raj B. Patel, Ian A. Walmsley, Markus Gr\"afe, Juan P. Torres, Enno Giese

item.title: Single-molecule strong optomechanical regimes in SERS via hybrid plasmonic cavities
item.description: arXiv:2608.03307v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify enhanced strong coherent Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) interactions facilitated by hybridized metallo-dielectric cavities with a resonant fluorescent molecule. By illuminating a detuned electronic transition near saturation via a narrowband hybrid plasmonic mode, we observe enhanced splittings in the Stokes and anti-Stokes spectra, revealing strong optomechanical coupling and nonlinear vibrational modifications at intensities far below irreversible SERS damage thresholds. We compute the second-order photon correlations that allows identifying the nonclassical character associated to these strong optomechanical interactions and SERS configurations that enables them to optically characterize the anharmonic character of the vibrational modes.
item.dc:creator: Miguel \'A. Mart\'inez-Garc\'ia, Johannes Feist, Diego Mart\'in-Cano

item.title: Millisecond optical coherence and strong collective coupling in an integrated telecom rare-earth photonic platform
item.description: arXiv:2608.08221v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long-range quantum network nodes require the combination of strong light-matter coupling, long coherence times and in-situ spectral control at telecom wavelengths. The coherence of erbium in integrated devices is held back by its hosts, which do not simultaneously provide the weakly magnetic nuclear-spin environment and the well-defined substitutional sites found in coherence-optimised bulk crystals. Here we bring such an optimised crystal onto a photonic chip, by bonding an Er${^{3+}}$:CaWO${_{4}}$ host without an adhesive interlayer to a high-${Q}$ electro-optically tuneable thin-film lithium niobate microring resonator. At an effective temperature of 75mK and a field of only 0.2T, ions probed through a waveguide show an effective homogeneous linewidth of ${289\pm5}$Hz (${T_{\text{M}}=1.10\pm0.02}$ms), with spectral diffusion proceeding at ${86\pm18}$Hz and saturating at ${1.5\pm0.2}$kHz. Electro-optically tuning the resonator through the erbium optical transition resolves an avoided crossing with a collective cooperativity of ${C=6.7\pm0.4}$ at zero field and ${C=4.9\pm0.2}$ at 0.4T, where ${T_{\text{M}}}$ exceeds 1ms. Exploiting superhyperfine coupling to the host's ${^{183}}$W nuclear spins, we store and retrieve optical phase information over 5s with a visibility of ${0.935\pm0.015}$. Strong collective coupling, millisecond coherence and in-situ spectral tuning in a single device thus establish heterogeneous integration leveraging coherence-optimised hosts as a route to scalable telecom quantum networks.
item.dc:creator: Kah Jen Wo, Pavel A. Dmitriev, Karthik Dasigi, Fumiya Hanamura, Steven Touzard

item.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
item.description: arXiv:2611.05355v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every nonlinearity is a quadratic detection (an interference, a balanced interferometric reading or a camera) and the output is a Born probability: attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^2$, the form of the Born rule, normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout; between detections a classical controller squares, divides, rescales and re-encodes. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-13}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference the model reaches 77.45 +- 0.91 % test accuracy, level within the spread of three seeds with a softmax transformer of the same size (76.62 +- 0.36 %). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 44 % of test pairs, out of the 53 % any single deletion can change, against 32 % for the softmax model's integrated gradients and 31 % for the Born Transformer's own attention. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics (simulated), and its attention overlaps to Hadamard tests on qubits; a separate coherent attention layer becomes one post-selected circuit (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps, the device gave the model's answers on the two shortest test pairs, also when the one word that decides one of them was deleted; with calibration circuits as deep as the overlaps, each word's evidence with the device's attention row sums followed the exact evidence on one pair (correlation 0.997) and on the other less closely (0.962).
item.dc:creator: Teerawat Tongloy, Jiraporn Pongsopa, Rangsan Jomtarak
